findings.issue_text: [BUG] header.scss calls @include flexbox()/align-items()/order() without any @import of common/foundation/mixins, so SCSS compilation fails with "Undefined mixin" unless some file already globally imports mixins.scss. The stylesheet build (assets:precompile / dev reload) aborts with a Sass "Undefined mixin 'flexbox'" error at header.scss, breaking the entire stylesheet bundle, not just the header — unless every consumer imports the mixin file in this diff, which none do.

[BUG] topic-post.scss invokes @include flexbox()/align-items() with no @import "common/foundation/mixins" in this file, relying on an implicit global import that this diff does not establish. If mixins.scss is not imported by topic-post.scss's dependency chain, Sass raises "Undefined mixin 'flexbox'" and the whole stylesheet bundle fails to compile.

[BUG] topic.scss invokes @include order(2) with no @import of the file defining @mixin order (mixins.scss), so the mixin must resolve via a global import this diff never adds. Sass "Undefined mixin 'order'" compile failure for the stylesheet bundle if the import chain doesn't already include mixins.scss.

[BUG] badges.css.scss invokes @include inline-flex()/align-items() with no @import "common/foundation/mixins" in the file, converting a previously plain-CSS rule into a compile-time dependency on a mixin this diff does not wire up here. Sass "Undefined mixin 'inline-flex'" compile failure if the mixin file isn't already in the import graph for this stylesheet.

[ADVISORY] -ms-align-items: $alignment; in the align-items mixin is a fabricated property — no browser ever supported -ms-align-items (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already emitted on the previous line), so this line is always invalid and discarded. No user-visible breakage (CSS parsers drop unknown declarations), but it signals the mixin was copied from an unvetted source; future maintainers may assume IE support matrices the mixin does not actually provide, and any strict CSS linter in the build pipeline flags this line.

[ADVISORY] Converting .contents to a flex container with no flex-wrap or min-width handling drops the previous float-based stacking behavior for narrow viewports. On small screens or with long site titles/category badges, the title, extra-info, and panel flex items no longer wrap; content overflows or gets clipped horizontally in the header where the old float layout stacked, and nothing in the diff verifies the responsive/narrow-width case.

[ADVISORY] Replacing .small-action-desc's fixed 4em left padding (which cleared the ~30px avatar) with percentage-only padding removes the avatar indentation entirely, with no min-width/gap guarantee between the flex sibling .topic-avatar and the text. At narrow widths the 1.5% padding approaches zero and the uppercase description text butts directly against the topic-avatar, degrading readability; the diff contains no check of the small-action layout at small container widths.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, a property that exists in no browser's implementation (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, which is emitted on the adjacent line). The invalid declaration is dead code that misleads the next maintainer into thinking -ms-align-items is a real IE vendor prefix, making future mixin edits (e.g., someone 'fixing' or copying the pattern) error-prone.

[BUG] The .small-action-desc padding change from '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' to '0 1.5%' removes the 4em left indent that compensated for the topic-avatar column, changing the rendered layout of every small-action (topic closed, deleted user, small-action banners) with no connection to header layout performance. Users see small-action descriptions shift left into the avatar column on every topic; this visual regression is invisible in a header-focused review and is not traceable to the stated PR intent.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the margin-top:5px on .small-action-desc p, margin:5px→0 on the inner p, and padding-top:4px on > p — pure visual restyling of small-action text spacing that no requirement in this PR covers. Anyone relying on this PR being a scoped header-performance change gets an unrequested global restyle of small-action typography; regressions here get reverted along with the header work.

[ADVISORY] The old `.title { float: left; }` rule is deleted outright rather than converted, and the .panel gets a hand-tuned `@include order(3)` while .extra-info-wrapper in topic.scss gets `@include order(2)` and no child ever gets order(1) — the ordering invariant is split across two files with an implicit default-order sibling. The next header change has three places to coordinate (header.scss contents/panel, topic.scss extra-info-wrapper) plus an unstated order-1 default; a reorder or insertion breaks silently with no single source of truth for the flex child order.

[ADVISORY] The `line-height: 1.5` added to .extra-info-wrapper and the removal of the `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` override are untraceable to the stated header-flexbox-performance intent — they are a separate vertical-rhythm adjustment bundled into the same diff. The bullet-badge alignment fix (margin-top compensation) and the line-height change are scope drift that makes bisecting any future header layout regression point at the wrong commit.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin forwards the modern flexbox keyword verbatim into the legacy 2009/-ms syntaxes, which use a different value vocabulary. -webkit-box-align: flex-start / flex-stretch / etc. are invalid in the old spec (valid values are start/end/center/stretch/baseline), so any future caller passing a modern keyword gets silently dropped declarations in old-IE/old-Android; today's callers (center, baseline) happen to be the intersection set, so the trap is armed but not yet sprung — the first caller using flex-start gets a silently unaligned layout in legacy browsers.

[ADVISORY] The panel is positioned via order(3) while .extra-info-wrapper gets order(2) in topic.scss, but .title and .contents' other children get no order, splitting the ordering contract for one flex container across two files with no shared definition. The next dev who reorders header children must discover that ordering is spread between header.scss (.panel order 3) and topic.scss (.extra-info-wrapper order 2) plus DOM-order defaults; the .contents flex container's layout rules now live in two stylesheets, and a change in one file silently reflows the other's layout (e.g., bumping .panel to order 1 does not move it before extra-info because that order lives elsewhere).

[BUG] Making .small-action a flex container leaves the floated .topic-avatar (float behavior inside flex items is undefined/ignored) and drops the 4em left padding that previously reserved space for the 45px avatar, replacing it with padding: 0 1.5% on .small-action-desc. Small-action rows (topic closed/archived/deleted notices) with an avatar now overlap or mis-space the avatar against the description text, since float inside a flex container is ignored and 1.5% of a narrow container under-reserves the avatar width.

[ADVISORY] Switching .contents to flexbox while .valign-helper (whose only purpose is the old vertical-centering hack) is retained creates a parallel layout mechanism for the same container. Maintainers now must reason about flex alignment and the valign-helper spacer simultaneously; the valign-helper becomes dead weight once flex is active but remains in the DOM/CSS, so removing it later requires re-auditing every header variant — a duplication that makes the next layout change riskier rather than easier.

[BUG] The PR's stated intent is a performance optimization (flexbox mixins), but it silently deletes the .small-action-desc left padding of 4em and replaces it with 1.5% padding, plus removes margin-top: 5px — a visual redesign, not a perf change. Every small-action row (topic close/archive/flags notices) visibly shifts: the description text no longer clears the 45px avatar and instead squeezes to 1.5% from the container edge, causing text to overlap/abut the avatar on narrow screens; users see unannounced visual regressions with no acceptance of the new layout.

[ADVISORY] The .extra-info-wrapper change removes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` compensation for bullet-style category badges while adding line-height: 1.5 — an unstated visual change hidden inside a 'performance' PR. Bullet-style category badges lose their 5px vertical offset and gain a new line-height, shifting title-row alignment on every topic page; a maintainer accepting this PR for its perf claim unknowingly accepts a layout redesign.

[ADVISORY] The `.title { float: left; }` rule is deleted outright rather than replaced, leaving .title with no display/float definition of its own inside the new flex container. .title relies entirely on flex-item defaults now; any consumer that styled .title expecting float context (e.g., clearing siblings, or plugins/themes overriding the float) silently breaks; the objective changed from 'keep title floated, use flex for perf' to 'remove the float' without that being flagged in the intent.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes `margin: 5px 0` → `margin: 0` on `p` inside .small-action-desc-inner and deletes `padding-top: 4px` on `> p`, further visual changes bundled into the perf PR with no stated rationale. Paragraphs inside small-action descriptions (e.g., moderator close messages) lose all vertical rhythm, running text lines together; the visual behavior change ships without any explicit acceptance of the new spacing.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite of `.bullet` from native `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline` to the prefixed mixins adds a `-moz-box`/`-ms-flexbox` legacy codepath that did not exist before, changing rendering on old engines from 'no flex' to '2009-spec flex' with different baseline semantics. Users on old Firefox/IE get a newly-active (and differently-behaving) 2009 flexbox layout for badge bullets — `-webkit-box-align: baseline` maps to different alignment semantics than modern `align-items: baseline` — introducing a behavior change on legacy browsers that the original code deliberately avoided by using only the modern syntax.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real CSS property in any IE version (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above), so it is dead code that browsers silently discard. No user-facing breakage, but the next developer editing flex alignment in DevTools or debugging old-IE quirks will waste time reasoning about a property that never applied, and the mixin invites cargo-cult copying of the phantom prefix into new code.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
